items.prompt: Why are inherited open lower/upper bounds sufficient on a proper tree?

options.text: They retain the intersection of all ancestor side constraints.
options.why: Every ancestor left/right inequality remains represented along the path.

options.text: Only the immediately preceding visited value matters.
options.why: Traversal order alone is not the invariant used by this bound-carrying source.

options.text: Each node's value is compared only with the root.
options.why: Intermediate ancestors can impose tighter constraints too.

options.text: All descendants must lie outside the root's numeric range.
options.why: Subtree constraints define appropriate open intervals, not an outside range.
